newsitem.title: AUSTRALIA: Australia's largest state re-elects conservatives.
newsitem.headline: Australia's largest state re-elects conservatives.

text.p: Australia's largest state, Western Australia, on Saturday re-elected a conservative government with an increased majority.
The conservative Liberal-National government headed by state premier Richard Court had been expected to win a landslide victory against the Labor opposition.
But with most of the votes counted by early Sunday, the Liberal-National coalition only increased its majority from seven to 11.
The election in a state where outback desert occupies an area almost the size of Argentina, and which is home to one of the country's largest aboriginal populations, was fought on local issues.
During the four-week long campaign the government ran heavily on its economic record, while Labor highlighted hospital waiting lists, dirty schools and crime in the suburbs.
Conservative governments are now in power nationally in Australia and in five of the country's six states and both its autonomous territories.
